scenarios.title: Carrier Parents
scenarios.evidence: Two dominant-phenotype parents have an aa child, so both must supply a and therefore are Aa.
scenarios.predictionPrompt: Does a dominant phenotype uniquely identify a genotype?
predictions: It can be AA or Aa
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Explain the genotype evidence, the probabilities and any uncertainty.
scenarios.keyIdea: A fictional single autosomal locus with complete dominance and full penetrance is assumed. Probability is not a guaranteed count.
hints: Each parent contributes one allele. A recessive aa outcome requires an a from each parent.
A dominant phenotype can be AA or Aa. Keep both possibilities unless other evidence rules one out.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: An aa child needs an a from each dominant parent, so both are Aa. The cross gives 25/50/25 genotypes per offspring, not a fixed family count.

scenarios.title: Recessive × Carrier

scenarios.teacherReasoning: aa supplies a on each row and Aa supplies A or a on columns. The square gives 50% Aa and 50% aa per offspring.

scenarios.title: Possible Dominant Parent
scenarios.answer: A single percentage is not justified until the dominant parent's genotype is known.
scenarios.predictionPrompt: Does a dominant phenotype uniquely identify a genotype?
predictions: It can be AA or Aa
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Explain the genotype evidence, the probabilities and any uncertainty.
scenarios.keyIdea: A fictional single autosomal locus with complete dominance and full penetrance is assumed. Probability is not a guaranteed count.
hints: Each parent contributes one allele. A recessive aa outcome requires an a from each parent.
A dominant phenotype can be AA or Aa. Keep both possibilities unless other evidence rules one out.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: aa × AA gives 0% recessive and aa × Aa gives 50%. The dominant parent could have either genotype, so one probability is unjustified.

scenarios.title: Independent Outcomes
scenarios.answer: The next outcome is not due; the same 25/50/25 probabilities apply to each pregnancy in this simplified model.
scenarios.predictionPrompt: Do earlier offspring outcomes make a different outcome due next?
predictions: Yes; a missing outcome is now due
No; the probabilities remain the same
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Calculate the next-offspring probabilities and explain why earlier outcomes do not make a particular genotype due.
scenarios.keyIdea: Under this independent-offspring model, each offspring has the same probabilities regardless of earlier outcomes.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: The Aa × Aa probabilities remain 25/50/25 for the next offspring. Previous outcomes do not make another due.

scenarios.title: Underdetermined Pedigree
scenarios.answer: aa × AA gives 0% recessive phenotype; aa × Aa gives 50%. Both crosses are possible; no single probability is justified.
